chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind one whom I am pleased with, do I recite behind him? He said: 'If you are pleased with him, do not recite behind him.'

key_terms.أَرْتَضِي بِهِ: I am pleased with him (referring to the validity/qualifications of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Do I recite Surah Al-Fatihah behind the Imam in congregational prayer if I am satisfied with his validity?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *qira'ah khalf al-imam* (recitation behind the Imam), establishing that a satisfied follower remains silent rather than reciting independently. This ruling underscores the sufficiency of the Imam's recitation for the congregation, distinguishing Shia practice from other schools where independent recitation is often required or recommended.
